title:
Comment of Shawn Kelm in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/22/2026

documents.name: 151805.txt
documents.text:
Shawn Kelm, Homer, AK.
DeepGreen Cook Inlet SVP LLC’s proposed data hub flies fundamentally counter to the desires of Alaskans and existing precedent which prioritizes our access to natural resources. The data hub would have significant deleterious impacts on fish species, namely salmon whose homing abilities are severely hampered by copper, which is allegedly a significant component in the proposed equipment. Not only are salmon commercially important to the people of this region, but they are also important for subsistence fishers, personal use, and the generation of tourism which is vital to the region. Disruption of this resource by the proposed data hub would cause significant strife to people who already experience higher costs than elsewhere in the country. In addition to the inevitable consequences for salmon, the data center is likely to be harmful to marine mammals, some of which are endangered, who depend on both salmon and clean waters with clear paths for migration. Furthermore, this proposed data center is completely counter to how Alaskans want the land and ocean to be used. We do not value data centers, we do not value the storage of electronic information, rather we value our natural resources and the preservation of pristine habitat. This does not mean that we do not value jobs and responsible exploitation of our resources, but that is not what this data center would do. It wouldn’t produce tangible goods that benefit Alaskans, rather it is the exportation of the waste and problems generated by technology to some location that is perceived to be the middle of nowhere and therefore somehow acceptable to trash. Furthermore, I cannot see how this data center would benefit Alaskans in the long term, and I believe the proposed location to be ill suited to the purpose. Cook Inlet experiences extremely large tidal swings, some of the largest in the world, combined with the high levels of soft sediment in the area this would be extremely hard on the proposed equipment. The well-known corrosive and abrasive characteristics of tidal soft sediment would undoubtedly cause damage to the equipment and cause copper, which as mentioned above is harmful to salmon’s ability to find their natal streams, to be released into the water. While I am of the opinion that this data center should not be built at all, I think that if it is going to become a reality, it should be placed elsewhere, and outside of Alaska’s extreme and largely pristine environment. I feel that if DeepGreen were truly confident in the safety and minimal environmental impact of this data hub, they wouldn’t be seeking to put it so far from the East Coast that all of its leadership calls home. Additionally, this proposal has proceeded as far as it has shows a blatant disregard for or ignorance of the history of this type of development as it relates to salmon, Washington, Oregon, and California are clear examples of the consequences of developing waters important to salmon. Let’s not make the same mistake here please. I have spent my whole life fishing for salmon that pass-through Cook Inlet, and I hope to pass that tradition to future generations, and I firmly believe that hope will not be realized if this type of development is allowed to occur in Alaska. This data hub is just the first step in that process, and we cannot allow it to be realized. 

Alaskans value common sense, not artificial intelligence.
